question.text: If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>b</mi></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>5</mn><mi>m</mi></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>c</mi></mrow></msup><msup><mi>y</mi><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>e</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfenced close="|" open="|" separators="|"><mtable columnalign="left"><mtr><mtd><mn>5</mn><mi>m</mi></mtd><mtd><mn>3</mn><mi>b</mi></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi></mtd><mtd><mn>4</mn><mi>d</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable></mfenced><mo>,</mo></math> <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfenced close="|" open="|" separators="|"><mtable columnalign="left"><mtr><mtd><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mtd><mtd><mn>5</mn><mi>m</mi></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn>3</mn><mi>c</mi></mtd><mtd><mn>2</mn><mi>n</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable></mfenced></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mfenced close="|" open="|" separators="|"><mtable columnalign="left"><mtr><mtd><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi></mtd><mtd><mn>3</mn><mi>b</mi></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd><mn>3</mn><mi>c</mi></mtd><mtd><mn>4</mn><mi>d</mi></mtd></mtr></mtable></mfenced><mo>,</mo></math> then the values of <math><mi>x</mi></math> and <math><mi>y</mi></math> are

options.text: <math><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mfenced><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mfrac><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mfenced></math>

solution.text:
Taking log in both the equations, we get, 
2alog⁡x+3blog⁡y=5m
3clog⁡x+4dlog⁡y=2n
By Cramer’s Rule, 
log⁡x=Δ1Δ3⇒x=eΔ1Δ3
log⁡y=Δ2Δ3⇒y=eΔ2Δ3
